title: Club sidemen, four years at the Howard, and dropping the club
summary: He recalls a Post Office alto player, Jeff on piano and the Lion, stayed three or four years at the Howard and gave up the violent club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who was in your band at that time?
I'm trying to think was there anybody that finally made good, or was pretty good. I remember one guy who worked in the Post Office. He played alto sax, he -- Toby. Toby.

Naw, no, no. He was fair. He's -- I don't know. He owned the horn, I would say, you know. (Laughs.) And Jeff -- what was Jeff's last name -- on piano. He smoked a big cigar like -- let's see, who died? The man? Willie Willard the Lion, yeah, but he was -- I'm trying to think who was the drummer.
How long did you go on playing both the club and the Howard?
Oh, I worked the Howard Theater about four years.
Yeah, stayed about three -- three or
You worked at the club for four years too?

No, no. I finally put the club down, because there was too much -- talking about violence, man, oh shoot. It was too much happening, you know, in there, for one thing, and then there was too much work, you know. I'd rather go and play the theater, go and take care of the theater and let the other thing go.
